name: Calder & Murn Houndstooth Sport Coat
description:
Calder & Murn is a mid-tier tailoring house out of Milwaukee's Tier 3 professional corridor, known for doing traditional men's and women's suiting without the corponation markup. The Houndstooth Sport Coat is their most recognizable piece — a structured single-button jacket in a cream-and-charcoal houndstooth pattern woven from a wool-viscose blend that holds its shape through a long transit commute. The lapels are notched and moderate, the chest pocket is functional, the interior has two slip pockets and one with a button flap. Lining is a deep burgundy microweave that catches the light when the jacket opens.

This is the jacket a mid-level project manager wears to a client meeting when they want to look put-together without looking corporate. It reads as thoughtful rather than flashy — someone who chose this deliberately. The cut is relaxed enough that it doesn't feel like armor. You see it at Tier 3 restaurants, at gallery openings in the transit district, at university faculty events. It's not trying to signal anything except that you know what you're doing.
what_it_says: You have taste, you have enough money to exercise it, and you didn't need a logo to prove either.
story_hooks: A Calder & Murn sport coat turns up in a Tier 1 pawn shop — the interior button-flap pocket has a folded note inside that shouldn't exist.
Calder & Murn is quietly being acquired by a corponation that plans to gut the workshop and replace production with automated fabrication — the last human-sewn run is already being made.
Someone is wearing this jacket at every single meeting before a string of Tier 3 contract murders; witnesses remember the houndstooth but nothing else.

physical_description.visual_profile: A structured yet approachable single-button sport coat with classical tailoring. The cream-and-charcoal houndstooth pattern reads as deliberately understated—professional without corporate edge. Sits comfortably on the shoulders with a subtle drape through the torso. Projects quiet confidence rather than status.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed tailored. Generous through the chest and shoulders, with a gentle taper at the waist. Sleeve length hits at the wrist bone. Not compression-fit or oversized—designed for layering and movement during transit commutes.
physical_description.primary_material: Wool-viscose blend woven in a traditional houndstooth pattern. The blend balances structure and breathability—viscose adds drape and recovery, wool holds shape through wear.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, densely woven face with a subtle tooth. Microweave lining inside (deep burgundy) is soft and catches light with subtle iridescence. No synthetic sheen—deliberately matte finish.
physical_description.color_scheme: Cream and charcoal in a classic houndstooth check. Interior lining is deep burgundy microweave that creates visual depth when the jacket opens or moves.
physical_description.closures: Single button closure at the chest (likely matte gunmetal or bone). Functional button flaps on interior chest and hip pockets.
distinctive_features: Notched lapels in moderate width—not aggressive or conservative
Functional chest pocket with subtle topstitching
Two interior slip pockets plus one button-flap security pocket
Burgundy microweave lining with subtle light-catching quality
Reinforced seams at stress points—made for frequent wear
No visible branding or logos—confidence through craft
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 Professional. Signals someone who has moved past entry-level but hasn't ascended to corpo wealth. The price point and construction quality position this as aspirational working-class—accessible luxury.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by project managers, junior academics, gallery curators, mid-level engineers, and transit district professionals. Signals intentional personal style without performative status-signaling. The wearer chose this jacket because they understand tailoring, not because they needed to prove something.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but well-maintained. Slight softening at the elbows and collar from regular wear. Creases at the button from repeated fastening. Shows character rather than wear—a jacket that improves slightly with age.
